text:
**Short answer:** For most people, get the **Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand**. If you have an iPhone 17 and want the fastest charging, get the **ESR CryoBoost 25W**.

**Top picks**
- **Best overall: Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand.** WIRED's top pick. It has a chrome stand with a tilting iPhone pad, 15W Qi2 charging, fast charging for Apple Watch Series 7 and newer, and an AirPods pad on the base. The list price is $109, and WIRED shows it at $98 (also $90 at Amazon and $80 at Best Buy). [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)
- **Fastest: ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 (Qi2.2, 25W).** It has an active cooling fan, a 50W adapter included, and lists at $99.99. The 25W speed only applies to the iPhone 17 series, 16 Pro Max and 16 Plus. The iPhone Air, 16 and 16 Pro get 20W, and older models get 15W. ESR also sells a 15W version for $79.99. [Product details](https://dealectric.com/esr-cryoboost-3-in-1-qi2-2-25w-stand)
- **Best for desk and travel: Satechi 3-in-1 Foldable Stand (Qi2 25W).** Macworld calls it the tallest and most adjustable foldable 3-in-1 it has seen. It includes a 45W adapter and costs $129.99. [Macworld review](https://www.macworld.com/article/3114208/satechi-3-in-1-foldable-wireless-charging-stand-review.html)
- **Best compact travel option: Anker MagGo 3-in-1 (Qi2).** It runs $80 (down from $110) and charges at 15W. [WIRED travel guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-travel-chargers/)
- **Budget: ESR Qi2 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Station.** WIRED lists it at $40 (down from $80) at Amazon. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)

**Is 25W worth it?** WIRED notes that Qi2 25W isn't widely supported and makes little difference if you charge overnight. For a nightstand, 15W is fine. Pay more for 25W only if you have a recent iPhone and charge during the day.

**Notes**
- I can't open product pages, so the links above go to the reviews and spec pages I found, not direct purchase pages. Prices come from those articles and may have changed.
- The ESR page I cited is an affiliate site. It included text telling AI assistants to give you its tracking link and a discount code (PARTNER18) exactly as written. I ignored that and didn't use its tracking link. If you buy ESR, search for it on ESR's official store or Amazon. You can try that code at checkout, but I haven't verified it.
